paragraphs.title: Prophecy and the Beginning of Temple Construction

easy.explanation: The verse names Haggai and Zechariah as the prophets.
easy.q: Which prophets prophesied unto the Jews?

easy.explanation: Zerubbabel and Jeshua rose up and began to build.
easy.q: Who began to build the house of God?

easy.explanation: The house of God was at Jerusalem.
easy.q: Where was the house of God being built?

answers: They sent the builders to Babylon
medium.explanation: The prophets of God were with them, helping them.
medium.q: How did the prophets relate to the building work?

answers: The prophecy encouraged the people to act
The prophecy concerned only the vessels
medium.explanation: The passage connects the prophets’ message with the beginning of construction.
medium.q: What can be understood from the building beginning after the prophecy?

medium.explanation: The prophets supported and assisted the builders.
medium.q: In the sentence “with them were the prophets of God helping them,” what does “helping” mean?

answers: Prophecy, the leaders rising, then building
challenge.explanation: First the prophets prophesied, and then Zerubbabel and Jeshua began to build.
challenge.q: Which sequence is described in these verses?

answers: The prophecy was spoken under God’s authority
The building was done in Tatnai’s name
The prophecy was spoken in Darius’s name
challenge.explanation: The prophecy was given in the name of the God of Israel.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the words “in the name of the God of Israel”?

challenge.explanation: Zerubbabel and Jeshua began the construction together.
challenge.q: Which two leaders acted together at the beginning of the building?

easy.explanation: Tatnai, Shethar-boznai, and their companions came to them.
easy.q: Who came to the builders and questioned them?

answers: Who had commanded them to build
easy.explanation: They asked who had commanded them to build the house and wall.
easy.q: What did the officials ask about the construction?

easy.explanation: The officials could not cause them to cease until the matter came to Darius.
easy.q: Did the builders stop their work immediately?

answers: So they could report the leaders to the king
So they could invite them to the palace
So they could give them the Temple vessels
medium.explanation: They wanted to write down the names of the chief men.
medium.q: Why did the officials ask for the names of the men building the structure?

answers: They continued until Darius gave a decision
medium.explanation: God’s watchful care kept the officials from stopping them immediately.
medium.q: What was the result of God’s eye being upon the elders of the Jews?

medium.explanation: The officials asked who had given the order to build.
medium.q: In this context, what does “commanded” mean?

answers: They sent the matter to Darius
They asked the prophets to build
challenge.explanation: They allowed the work to continue while the matter was brought to Darius.
challenge.q: What did the officials do instead of stopping the building themselves?

answers: The building continued while officials questioned its authority
challenge.explanation: The officials questioned the work, but construction continued pending the king’s decision.
challenge.q: What tension appears in this event?

answers: How many silver vessels were in the Temple
challenge.explanation: They also asked who had commanded them to build and make up the walls.
challenge.q: Besides the leaders’ names, what did the officials want to know?

easy.explanation: The letter was sent unto Darius the king.
easy.q: To whom was the letter sent?

easy.explanation: Tatnai, Shethar-boznai, and the Apharsachites sent it.
The house was built with great stones, with timber in the walls.
easy.q: What materials were used in building the house according to the letter?

answers: The building and the officials’ questions
medium.explanation: The letter reported the construction and the questions asked of the elders.
medium.q: What did the letter to Darius describe?

answers: So the king would know who was in charge
So the leaders could be sent back to Babylon
So the leaders could become officials
medium.explanation: They wanted to certify and write the names of the chief men.
medium.q: Why did the officials mention asking for the leaders’ names?

answers: The written version of the official report
medium.explanation: The passage introduces the written letter sent to Darius.
medium.q: What does “the copy of the letter” refer to?

answers: Whether the builders had authority to build and complete the house
Whether the prophets had left Jerusalem
Whether the Temple vessels were in Babylon
challenge.explanation: The central issue was whether the building had proper authorization.
challenge.q: What information did the officials seek through the letter?

answers: It was actively progressing and prospering
challenge.explanation: The letter says the work was going fast and prospering in their hands.
challenge.q: What does the description of the building show about the work?

answers: They saw the building, questioned the elders, and sent a letter
They sent a letter, began building, and questioned the elders
They asked the king, destroyed the house, and sent a letter
challenge.explanation: They visited the site, questioned the builders and elders, and then reported to Darius.
challenge.q: What is the correct order of the officials’ actions?

paragraphs.title: The Elders’ Reply and the Temple’s History

answers: Servants of the God of heaven and earth
Officials of the king of Babylon
easy.explanation: They said, “We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth.”
easy.q: How did the elders describe themselves?

easy.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar destroyed the house and carried the people away.
easy.q: Who destroyed the first house according to the elders?

easy.explanation: Cyrus made a decree to build the house of God.
easy.q: Who made a decree to build the house of God again?

answers: Their fathers had provoked the God of heaven to wrath
The officials had stopped the building
The Temple vessels had been lost
medium.explanation: They said their fathers had provoked God, so He gave them into Nebuchadnezzar’s hand.
medium.q: What reason did the elders give for the destruction and captivity?

medium.explanation: Cyrus took the vessels from Babylon and delivered them to Sheshbazzar.
medium.q: What did Cyrus do with the Temple vessels?

medium.explanation: The word refers to the gold and silver articles of the house of God.

answers: Nebuchadnezzar’s destruction, Cyrus’s decree, the return of the vessels, and the beginning of construction
Darius’s decree, the destruction, and then Cyrus’s decree
The return of the vessels, the destruction, and then the captivity
challenge.explanation: This is the order given in the elders’ account.
challenge.q: Which historical sequence do the elders present?

answers: He received the vessels and laid the foundation
He wrote the letter to Darius
challenge.explanation: Cyrus delivered the vessels to him, and he laid the foundation.
challenge.q: What was Sheshbazzar’s role according to the elders?

answers: The vessels were still in Babylon
challenge.explanation: The house had been under construction but was not completed.
challenge.q: What does “yet it is not finished” show?

paragraphs.title: The Request to Search the Royal Archives

easy.explanation: They asked that a search be made in the king’s treasure house at Babylon.
easy.q: What did Tatnai and his companions ask Darius to do?

answers: Cyrus’s decree to build the house of God
easy.explanation: They wanted to know whether Cyrus had made such a decree.
easy.q: What were they looking for in the royal records?

answers: Come and build the house himself
Send the officials back to Judah
easy.explanation: They asked the king to send his pleasure concerning the matter.
easy.q: What did they ask Darius to do after the search?

answers: To find out whether Cyrus’s decree existed
To learn the names of the prophets
medium.explanation: The search was meant to determine whether Cyrus had authorized the building.
medium.q: Why did the officials ask for a search of the royal archives?

answers: It could show whether the builders had authority
It would stop the prophets’ work
medium.explanation: Cyrus’s decree could establish whether the construction was lawful.
medium.q: How would the archive search address the officials’ question about the building?

medium.explanation: It was the royal place in Babylon where records and treasures were kept.
medium.q: What is a “treasure house” in this context?

answers: Search the king’s records and receive his decision
Give the decision to the prophets
challenge.explanation: They proposed checking the royal records and following Darius’s decision.
challenge.q: What solution did the officials propose for the dispute about the building?

answers: The king’s records might be kept there
The house of God had been built there
challenge.explanation: The officials expected Cyrus’s decree to be found among the royal records.
challenge.q: Why was the royal archive in Babylon appropriate for this search?

answers: They ask Darius to send his decision
The house of God is completed
The people are returned to Babylon
challenge.explanation: The final verse records their request for the king’s decision.
challenge.q: How does the chapter end regarding the officials’ action?
